BILL NUMBER:  S3743

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to coordinated
assessment programs


 PURPOSE

The purpose of this bill is to promote intergovernmental cooperation
by clarifying and simplifying the administration of Coordinated
Assessment Programs (CAPs).

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill amends Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) § 579(1) to
clarify that any agreement to establish a CAP must be entered into at
least 45 days prior to the relevant taxable status date, and to delete
the current requirement that the governing body of the participating
assessing units must approve such agreement within that same time
frame.

Section 2 of the bill amends RPTL § 579(3)(a) to clarify that an
appointive assessor in a CAP is subject to the six-year term of office
set forth in RPTL § 310.

Section 3 of the bill makes the following changes to RPTL § 579(4):

* amends paragraph (b) to reduce from 6 months to 45 days the time
period prior to the relevant taxable status date that a governing body
of an assessing unit must notify the State Board of Real Property
Services that it intends to withdraw from a CAP;

* amends paragraph (c) to reduce from 6 months to 45 days the time
period prior to the relevant taxable status date that local laws or
resolutions providing for the termination of a· CAP must be approved;

* adds a new paragraph (d) to provide for the automatic termination of
a CAP in the event that the State Board of Real Property Services
becomes aware, on or before the relevant taxable status date, that the
same individual is no longer serving as assessor in all the assessing
units of a CAP; and

* adds a new paragraph (e) to provide that a CAP shall continue unless
it is terminated pursuant to the provisions of RPTL § 579(4)(c) or
(d).

Section 4 of the bill provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

RPTL § 579(1) provides that the governing body of two or more
assessing units may establish a CAP by entering into an agreement that
is approved by the governing body of each participating assessing unit
at least 45 days before the first assessment role to which such
program is to apply.

RPTL § 579(3)(a) provides that the same individual shall be appointed
assessor in each assessing unit participating in a CAP, but the
section does not specify a term of office for such individual.

RPTL § 579(4)(b) and (c) provide that a governing body of an assessing
unit participating in a CAP must notify the State Board of Real
Property Services at least six months prior to the relevant taxable

status date that it intends either to withdraw from or terminate a
CAP.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This legislative proposal was included in the proposed State Fiscal
Year 2008-2009 budget (S.6806 & A.9806, Part T, §§ 14-16), but it was
not included in the adopted budget.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

The CAP Program was established in 1994 to provide for administrative
efficiency in assessment. The Program, however, may be underutilized.
This bill reduces certain technical time requirements and clarifies
other procedures that govern the Program in an effort to encourage
more assessing units to participate. The expansion of the CAP Program
is an important step toward the overall goal of consolidating and
streamlining local assessment functions in order to control costs and
reduce property taxes.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

To the extent that this bill leads to greater participation in CAPs by
assessing units, additional State aid of up $7 per parcel may be
payable to each additional assessing unit participating in a CAP,
pursuant to RPTL § 1573.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The bill takes effect immediately.
